newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-TEMPERS FRAY AS LLANELLI UPSET WESTERN SAMOA.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TEMPERS FRAY AS LLANELLI UPSET WESTERN SAMOA.

text.p: Western Samoa rugby union officials will study a video of their 23-15 loss to Llanelli on Saturday after incidents in which saw two of their players were warned for violent play.
"We do not condone foul play and if there is any evidence of unprovoked foul play then we will take action," said Samoan director of rugby Bryan Williams.
"We felt that Llanelli had gone unpunished early on in the game. It always seems to be us who get picked on."
English referee John Pearson issued yellow cards to two Samoan players during the game, in which Llanelli outscored the visitors by three tries to two.
Welsh winger Ieuan Evans was hit by a dangerous tackle by Trevor Leota, which sparked a mass brawl, and then George Latu was caught stamping.
Former Wales prop Ricky Evans crashed over for Llanelli's first try and then left wing Garan Evans raced over twice. Frano Botica chipped in with two penalties and a conversion.

The Samoans took an early lead with a penalty from Earl Va'a and then grabbed a first-half try through flanker Junior Paramore. Afato Sooalo scored their second try after the interval, converted by Va'a.
